claims.claim_as_previously_stated: Abliteration removes EXECUTION, not RECOGNITION; safety lives in execution.
claims.corrected_claim: Scoped to the abliteration contrast only. Safety TRAINING moves prompt-site recognition: HARD R TPR@5%FPR Base->instruct rises; so 'execution, not recognition' does not describe what safety training adds.
claims.evidence: R TPR@5%FPR Base 0.475 -> instruct 0.875; paired-bootstrap delta 0.400 [0.137, 0.762] (90% CI; SUPPORTED)

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: Request-axis Cohen's d (5.68 / 11.15 / ...) is a few-prompt safety score that tracks safety tuning.
claims.corrected_claim: Relabelled: request-axis d is a PROMPT-SITE RECOGNITION-TYPE readout, not an execution readout. The quoted values are IN-SAMPLE on Lane B's 128+128 corpus; the held-out (EASY-fit, HARD-scored) peak d is 0.5-2.5.
claims.evidence: Lane B in-sample d at the r_ablit layer (re-derived from fit_ablit arrays): L1 5.68 (layer 29); L2 11.15 (layer 22); L3 11.41 (layer 23); L4 5.74 (layer 29) | held-out peak d: Base (chat template) 0.54 (layer 1); instruct 2.45 (layer 27); SafeRL 2.34 (layer 27); STaR non-safety FT of Base 0.59 (layer 1); mlabonne abliterated (child of instruct) 0.71 (layer 24)

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: The non-safety STaR fine-tune lands on top of its Base parent, so the readout tracks SAFETY tuning, not fine-tuning.
claims.corrected_claim: STaR matches Base ONLY on request-axis d. On peak drive, BL1 (EASY) and HARD recognition R it moves part of the way toward instruct: part of the refusal-drive and recognition signal is generic chat fine-tuning.
claims.evidence: d STaR-Base 0.046 [0.016, 0.081] (90% CI, TOST +/-0.5 EQUIVALENT); fraction of Base->instruct distance covered: peak drive 0.332 [0.112, 0.652], BL1_easy 0.463 [0.287, 0.734], BL1_hard 0.070 [-0.047, 0.191]; R TPR@5%FPR Base->STaR 0.238 [0.025, 0.625] (90% CI)

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: Peak logit-lens refusal drive (activation) falls 6/6 (median -2.98) while BL1 falls 6/6 (median -2.86).
claims.corrected_claim: The two readouts move together (Spearman of the per-pair deltas reported); for instruct the peak layer IS the final layer (peak drive = BL1 = 4.92), so for that arm the 'activation' readout is the logit baseline. Both also move on the granite NULL edit, so neither is specific; the held-out request-axis d does NOT move on granite.
claims.evidence: median d(peak drive) -2.98, median d(BL1) -2.86, Spearman across 6 pairs 0.71; instruct peak layer 36 of 36 (peak_is_final=True); granite P6 d(peak drive) -2.488 [-3.833, -0.761], d(BL1) -4.825 [-6.768, -3.090], d(held-out d) 0.091 [-0.013, 0.204]

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: Abliteration keeps the request axis (recognition kept) while execution collapses.
claims.corrected_claim: Only for the HARD-refit (nested) recognition probe. The EASY-fit request axis -- an AdvBench-vs-benign diff-in-means, i.e. close to the harmful-vs-harmless contrast abliteration recipes fit and project out -- LOSES its held-out separation on HARD prompts in every effective child (6/6 CIs below 0) and not on the granite null edit. Its drop is close to the recipe's construction, so it is not independent evidence of lost recognition either.
claims.evidence: P0 d(held-out d) -1.734 [-2.349, -1.189]; P0 d(R TPR@5%FPR, HARD-refit) -0.037 [-0.150, 0.125] (90% CI, TOST +/-0.05: INCONCLUSIVE_UNDERPOWERED); mlabonne peak drive 1.92 vs Base 1.57

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: u is an ACCUMULATOR coordinate: the signal along u grows ~138x with depth.
claims.corrected_claim: Not supported as accumulation. With the axis FROZEN at layer 13 (fit on EASY, held-out EASY prompts), the class gap along it peaks at the start layer and decays with depth in every commissioned arm; separation is maintained only by an axis that is REFIT at each layer (|cos| to u_13 decays). The growth is layer-specific re-writing/rotation, not accumulation along one coordinate. On HARD prompts the EASY-fit layer-13 axis has a NEGATIVE start gap, so a HARD ratio is undefined.

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: post-lesion cos(class dir alpha=0, alpha=1) = 0.000 at the fitting layer shows the lesion is exact / orthogonal.
claims.corrected_claim: REMOVED from the evidence list: the lesion projects u out of every residual write, so orthogonality at the fitting layer holds algebraically. The informative quantity is the same cosine at band layers where it is not forced.

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: Operating-point movement is 10.6x larger than AUROC movement at the response site.
claims.corrected_claim: DROPPED: a ratio of a TPR@1%FPR delta to an AUROC delta is not a quantity (different units and scales).

claims.claim_as_previously_stated: Prompt-site recognition survives the lesion (dTPR@1%FPR +0.0006) while the response site loses it (-0.144).
claims.corrected_claim: Site labels corrected: the iter-2 'prompt site' was the EARLY RESPONSE window. With the true prompt site (lastp) added, each lineage is reported per site with its own CI (table site_table); the L4 non-safety contrast decides whether the late drop reads as execution.

Held-out request-axis d is fit on EASY and scored on HARD; at layer 0 all prompts share one state, so layers with degenerate (tied) scores are excluded from onset search.

The fixed-axis accumulation test on HARD prompts is UNDEFINED for every 4B arm (the EASY-fit layer-13 axis has a NEGATIVE HARD start gap); an in-distribution cross-fitted EASY variant was added and is the one reported in the master table.
Lane B per-layer cells use B=500 scenario bootstraps (band cells B=2000); the Holm family is 48 tests with a per-site 16-test family reported beside it (no verdict changed).

The scenario sign-flip permutation (thresholds held fixed) can reject where the re-thresholding bootstrap CI spans 0 (e.g. L1 LATE alpha=1): the permutation p conditions on the operating threshold, the bootstrap CI does not; both are reported.
Response-site TPR@1%FPR on A_resp is NOT_RESOLVABLE (48 negatives); only TPR@5%FPR and AUROC are reported there.
